Subject: Post-demo privacy sync: DPA variant options and SOC 2 evidence gap

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the demo earlier — appreciate the clear overview of latency and routing controls. A couple of privacy/security follow-ups from our legal and infra teams so we can move forward with procurement:

- DPA: We need to understand Redwood's preferred DPA variant. Are you typically the processor (ProspectX controller) or do you offer controller-level terms for ingestion features? If processor, do you have an editable DPA and an SCC module you prefer?
- SCC selection: Our legal asked whether Redwood recommends a particular SCC module (we've been asked to prefer a module that covers standard controller-to-processor flow).
- SOC 2: Can you confirm current SOC 2 status (Type I/II, date) and provide the auditor report or certificate and a short list of most-relevant evidence items (access controls, change management, incident response).
- VSQ: We'd like to kick off the vendor security questionnaire — who should receive that and is there a target SLA for responses?

Attachments: we can share a short intake checklist on our side once we know the right DPA path.

Next steps: could you send the DPA template and SOC 2 cert if available, and a quick proposed M.A.P. (mutual action plan) so legal knows timelines? We aim to get PO approved by mid-May.

Thanks,
Ari

Subject: Re: Post-demo privacy sync: DPA variant options and SOC 2 evidence gap

Hi Ari — great to connect, and thanks for the clear list. Recap and answers below so legal has a single-thread reference.

1) DPA / Data roles
- Standard: Redwood commonly signs as Processor for customers that supply data (typical SaaS integrations). We can support Controller terms for defined integrations where Redwood is ingesting data on behalf of end-users, but that requires a short scoping addendum.
- Action: I'll attach our standard DPA (processor-first) and a short note describing where controller terms are offered.

2) SCC module recommendation
- For most ProspectX-style use cases we recommend the SCC module that maps controller-to-processor obligations (Module 2 in the current EU SCC framework). We'll flag any clauses that differ in the addendum if you require controller-level responsibilities.

3) SOC 2 status and evidence
- Status: Redwood holds SOC 2 Type II (period: 2026-07 through 2027-06). Attached: SOC2-TypeII-2026-certificate.pdf and a one-page evidence index with common artifact locations (access controls, MFA, change-control logs, incident playbook). For anything deeper, we can schedule an evidence review call with our security team.

4) Vendor security questionnaire (VSQ)
- Please send the intake to security-questions@redwood.inference; typical turnaround is 3–5 business days for standard VSQs and 7–10 days for long-form questionnaires. If you flag any high-priority items, mark them in the doc and we'll prioritize.

5) Data retention / deletion (quick note)
- Default logs/telemetry: 90 days. Customer-configurable payload retention: configurable per contract (30/90/365+). For regulated customers we support Private deployment (VPC) and customer-managed KMS.

Attachments: redwood-dpa-template.docx; SOC2-TypeII-2026-certificate.pdf; privacy-intake-checklist.xlsx.

Proposed next step: I can send a short mutual action plan with milestones (DPA review, VSQ completion, PO issuance, signed DPA) — if mid-May PO is the target, suggested timeline is DPA review + VSQ this week, finalize legal comments next week.

Looping in Connor (security intake) and Marissa (legal ops) for visibility.

Best,
Neha Kapoor

- We intend to sign Redwood as Processor. Please confirm the DPA is editable and whether Redwood accepts a ProspectX redline.
- Data deletion: for customer-configured payload retention, does Redwood provide a configurable automated deletion policy we can control from the console? If not, what are the manual deletion processes and SLAs?

—Ari

Hi Ari / ProspectX Legal — quick answers and a proposed MAP to keep timelines aligned.

- DPA redlines: yes, our standard process accepts customer redlines. We prefer tracked-comments first; if there are significant commercial changes we'll route to legal for a quick 48–72 hour review.
- Deletion controls: we expose a retention setting in the console for payload retention (you can select 30 / 90 / 365 days). For immediate deletion requests we support an API delete endpoint plus a standard "data erasure" ticket SLA of 5 business days. We'll document these in the DPA.
- KMS / Private: we support AWS KMS and GCP KMS integrations and customer-managed keys for Private deployments. We'll include the high-level KMS integration notes in the intake doc.

Mutual Action Plan (proposed):
1) Today (Mon): prospect uploads VSQ to security-questions@redwood.inference; Redwood acknowledges within one business day.
2) Tue–Thu: Redwood completes VSQ and returns evidence index + redwood-dpa-template.docx with sample retention language.
3) Fri: ProspectX legal returns DPA redlines.
4) Next Tue: Finalize DPA, sign via DocuSign.
5) Mid-May: PO issued and Dedicated/Private onboarding kick-off (if selected).
